record.context_brief: Kantorovich formulation and parsimonious optimal control
record.original_question: In the Kantorovich formulation of multi-agent control, where solutions are represented as measures on the space of continuous curves and related to the classical Lagrangian and Eulerian formulations, how can one characterize sparse or parsimonious controls and derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions within that framework?

evidence.quote: Along the same notes, we want to point to another recent contribution [29], where the authors, besides the classical Lagrangian and Eulerian point of view, consider the Kantorovich formulation. The latter is based on representing solutions to equations as measures over the space of continuous curves.
the authors present various equivalence and Γ-convergence results, but it would be interesting to understand sparsity, parsimonious controls, and necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-agent control system formulated in three equivalent ways:

1. (Lagrangian) A population of agents is described by trajectories $t\mapsto x_i(t)\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $i=1,\dots,N$, satisfying $\dot x_i(t)=v_F(t,x_i(t),\mu^N_t)+u_i(t)$, where $\mu^N_t=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\delta_{x_i(t)}$, $v_F:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is a given interaction field, and $u_i\in L^2([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$ are controls.

2. (Eulerian) The mean-field limit is described by a curve $t\mapsto\mu_t\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ together with a Borel velocity field $w:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ that decomposes as $w(t,x)=v_F(t,x,\mu_t)+u(t,x)$, satisfying the continuity equation $\partial_t\mu_t+\mathrm{div}(w\,\mu_t)=0$ in the sense of distributions, with prescribed initial datum $\mu_0$.

3. (Kantorovich) Solutions are represented as probability measures $\eta\in\mathcal{P}(\Gamma)$ on the space $\Gamma=C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$ of continuous curves, concentrated on absolutely continuous curves $\gamma$ that satisfy $\dot\gamma(t)=v_F(t,\gamma(t),(e_t)_\#\eta)+u_\eta(t,\gamma)$ for $\eta$-a.e. $\gamma$, where $e_t:\Gamma\to\mathbb{R}^d$ is the evaluation map $\gamma\mapsto\gamma(t)$, and $u_\eta$ is a control law that may depend on the curve.

Given a cost functional of the form
$$\mathcal{J}(\eta,u_\eta)=\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Gamma L(t,\gamma(t),(e_t)_\#\eta,u_\eta(t,\gamma))\,d\eta(\gamma)\,dt + \int_\Gamma\Psi(\gamma)\,d\eta(\gamma),$$
together with a sparsity-promoting term (for instance an $L^1$-type penalization of the control in a suitable sense), address the following:

(a) Provide a precise notion of "sparse" or "parsimonious" control within the Kantorovich formulation, namely a notion that captures the idea that only a small (in measure) portion of the population is actively controlled at any given time, and that is consistent under the equivalences with the Lagrangian and Eulerian formulations.

(b) Derive necessary optimality conditions (in the form of a Pontryagin-type maximum principle on $\mathcal{P}(\Gamma)$) for minimizers of $\mathcal{J}$ in the Kantorovich formulation, including the case with sparsity-promoting penalizations.

(c) Identify sufficient conditions (such as convexity/semiconcavity hypotheses on $L$, $\Psi$, and $v_F$) under which the necessary conditions in (b) are also sufficient for optimality.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not reveal a published treatment of sparsity, parsimonious controls, and necessary/sufficient optimality conditions specifically within the Kantorovich (measure-on-curves) formulation of multi-agent control. Related work establishes equivalence and Γ-convergence among Lagrangian, Eulerian and Kantorovich formulations, and separately treats sparse controls in the Lagrangian/Eulerian mean-field setting, but a combined treatment in the Kantorovich framework appears not to be available, so the problem is regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Mean-field optimal control (Kantorovich formulation)
status_evidence.snippet: Equivalence and Γ-convergence results among Lagrangian, Eulerian, and Kantorovich formulations are presented; sparsity and optimality conditions are mentioned as directions not yet developed.
status_evidence.claim: Sparsity and necessary/sufficient optimality conditions in the Kantorovich formulation are noted as open questions.
